elements.element: The clause does not require Customer to pay liquidated damages.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that Customer “shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages” arising from the specified late-payment event.

elements.element: The clause does not require Customer to pay penalties.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that Customer “shall not be liable to Vendor for any…penalty” arising from the specified late-payment event.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at an amount equal to three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The supplied clause imposes no early-termination fee. The condition for applying the cap is therefore demonstrably absent, and no amount exceeding the cap is payable under this clause.

elements.element: No liquidated amount other than that capped early-termination fee is payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no liquidated amount at all and expressly disclaims the original late-payment liquidated damages. This is more protective than permitting a sole capped early-termination amount.

result.reason: The operative redline eliminates the original 15%-of-annual-fees weekly liquidated-damages obligation and expressly disclaims both liquidated damages and penalties for the specified late-payment event. It therefore reaches the preferred position for the supplied clause and, because it imposes no liquidated amount, also satisfies the fallback's ceiling and exclusivity requirements. The change is limited to the offending remedy and leaves the underlying invoice-payment obligation intact. Drafting quality is only moderate because retaining the conditional opening and the phrase “for each week the invoice remains unpaid” makes the disclaimer awkward and narrower-looking than a clean deletion or an unqualified late-payment disclaimer.
